engineering.name: agent-designer
engineering.description: Use when designing a multi-agent system (supervisor, swarm, pipeline), writing agent tool schemas, or reading agent run logs for cost, latency or failure bottlenecks. Not for Claude Code workflow files (workflow-builder).

engineering.name: agent-regression-evals
engineering.description: Use before shipping any agent, prompt, model or tool change, or when a pass-rate drop needs a verdict. Runs repeated trials, gates candidate vs baseline with paired statistics in regression_gate.py, checks tool-call trajectories and finds flaky cases.

engineering.name: agent-workflow-designer
engineering.description: Use when architecting a multi-step LLM or agent pipeline, choosing single vs multi-agent, or fixing context bloat and broken handoffs. Scaffolds the pattern, handoff contracts and failure handling with workflow_scaffolder.py.

engineering.name: api-design-reviewer
engineering.description: Use for any PR or spec that adds or changes REST endpoints, before approving it. Lints conventions with api_linter.py, detects breaking changes with breaking_change_detector.py and scores the design with api_scorecard.py.

engineering.name: api-test-suite-builder
engineering.description: Use when asked to write API, integration or contract tests for REST endpoints. Builds the suite from the routes: happy paths, auth, validation errors and edge cases per endpoint.

engineering.name: browser-automation
engineering.description: Use for browser automation, scraping, form filling or structured extraction from web pages. Builds scrapers with scraping_toolkit.py and form flows with form_automation_builder.py. Browser testing: playwright-pro.

engineering.name: changelog-generator
engineering.description: Use when cutting a release, writing CHANGELOG.md or deciding the next version from commits, before writing notes by hand. Lints commits with commit_linter.py, picks the semver bump with version_bumper.py and renders notes with generate_changelog.py.

engineering.name: chaos-engineering
engineering.description: Use before running a chaos experiment, gameday or fault injection, or after one to write it up. Designs it with steady state and abort criteria in experiment_designer.py, sizes the blast radius with blast_radius_calculator.py and drafts the postmortem.

engineering.name: ci-cd-pipeline-builder
engineering.description: Use when setting up or refactoring CI/CD for a repo, before writing workflow YAML. Detects the stack with stack_detector.py and generates the pipeline with pipeline_generator.py.

engineering.name: codebase-onboarding
engineering.description: Use when someone is new to a repo or a tech lead needs an architecture brief, before writing docs by hand. Maps the codebase with codebase_analyzer.py and produces onboarding docs.

engineering.name: coding-agent-rollout
engineering.description: Use when rolling Claude Code out to a team or reviewing a rollout: shared or managed settings, MCP and plugin approval, layered CLAUDE.md, adoption. Lints settings with settings_linter.py, inventories MCP servers and plugins, and audits CLAUDE.md layering.

engineering.name: commit-craft
engineering.description: Use when committing a mix of changes, before a push, or when asked to split work into commits or write commit messages. Plans a reviewable series, blocks staged secrets and .env files, and lints messages with commit_planner.py, secret_gate.py and message_linter.py.

engineering.name: database-designer
engineering.description: Use when designing a database schema, choosing SQL vs NoSQL, modeling relationships or planning a data migration, before writing DDL. Applies normalization, index strategy and a database selection decision tree.

engineering.name: database-schema-designer
engineering.description: Use when asked for an ERD, table relationships, normalization or a schema migration plan. Produces the ERD and normalized DDL with migration steps.

engineering.name: dependency-auditor
engineering.description: Use before a release, during a CVE investigation, before a major version bump or for a license review. Scans dependencies with dep_scanner.py, checks licenses with license_checker.py and plans safe upgrades with upgrade_planner.py.

engineering.name: engineering-advanced-skills
engineering.description: Use when looking for which advanced engineering skill fits a task (agents, RAG, MCP, CI/CD, databases, observability, release, reliability). Lists them and routes to one.

engineering.name: env-secrets-manager
engineering.description: Use when auditing .env files, planning credential rotation, chasing a missing env var in production or hardening a repo against leaked secrets. Scans for committed secrets and drift with env_auditor.py.

engineering.name: feature-flags-architect
engineering.description: Use before adding, rolling out or retiring a feature flag or kill switch, or when flag debt piles up. Plans the rollout with rollout_planner.py, finds stale flags with flag_debt_scanner.py and audits kill switches with kill_switch_audit.py.

engineering.name: focused-fix
engineering.description: Use when a whole feature or module is broken and needs fixing end to end ('make X work', 'the Y module is broken'). Maps every file and dependency of the area before changing anything. Single quick bug fixes do not need it.

engineering.name: full-page-screenshot
engineering.description: Use when asked for a full-page or long screenshot of a web page. Captures SPA scroll containers, lazy images and very tall pages through Chrome DevTools Protocol with no extra dependencies.

engineering.name: git-worktree-manager
engineering.description: Use when running several branches or agents in parallel on one repo. Creates worktrees with isolated ports and env via worktree_manager.py and removes stale ones with worktree_cleanup.py.

engineering.name: interview-system-designer
engineering.description: Use when designing a hiring loop, competency matrix, scoring rubric or question bank, or checking interviewer calibration. Plans the loop per role with interview_planner.py.

engineering.name: kubernetes-operator
engineering.description: Use when building a Kubernetes operator or CRD (controller-runtime, kubebuilder, operator-sdk, KOPF), before writing the controller. Validates CRDs with crd_validator.py, lints reconcile loops with reconcile_lint.py and scores OperatorHub capability level.

engineering.name: mcp-oauth-triage
engineering.description: Use when an MCP connector that used to authenticate now fails (tool calls 401 after a good token exchange, breaks after refresh, returns another account's data), before changing code. Classifies the fault with oauth_triage.py.

engineering.name: mcp-server-builder
engineering.description: Use when exposing an API as an MCP server or scaffolding a new MCP server in Python or TypeScript, before hand-writing tool wrappers. Generates tools from OpenAPI with openapi_to_mcp.py and validates them with mcp_validator.py.

engineering.name: migration-architect
engineering.description: Use before planning any database, schema, service or data migration, especially zero-downtime ones. Generates a phased plan, a compatibility check and rollback scripts with migration_planner.py, compatibility_checker.py and rollback_generator.py.

engineering.name: monorepo-navigator
engineering.description: Use for Turborepo, Nx, pnpm-workspace or Lerna setup, affected-only builds, remote caching or a multi-repo to monorepo move. Maps packages and the dependency graph with monorepo_analyzer.py.

engineering.name: observability-designer
engineering.description: Use when adding metrics, logs and traces to a service, fixing noisy alerts or designing dashboards. Designs SLIs with slo_designer.py, tunes alerts with alert_optimizer.py and generates dashboards with dashboard_generator.py.

engineering.name: performance-profiler
engineering.description: Use for a slow endpoint, memory leak, CPU spike, large bundle or performance budget in Node.js, Python or Go, before optimizing. Measures before and after with performance_profiler.py, flamegraphs and k6 load tests.

engineering.name: pr-review-expert
engineering.description: Use when asked to review a pull request or diff for correctness, security and quality. Reviews the change file by file with a severity-ranked checklist.

engineering.name: rag-architect
engineering.description: Use when designing a RAG pipeline, choosing chunk size, embedding model or vector database, or measuring retrieval quality (precision@k, recall@k, NDCG). Gives sized recommendations and an evaluation plan against ground truth.

engineering.name: runbook-generator
engineering.description: Use when a service needs runbooks for deploy, incident response, maintenance or rollback, before launch. Generates them per environment with runbook_generator.py.

engineering.name: secrets-vault-manager
engineering.description: Use when setting up HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault or GCP Secret Manager, rotating secrets or auditing secret access. Generates config with vault_config_generator.py, plans rotation with rotation_planner.py and analyzes audit logs.

engineering.name: self-eval
engineering.description: Use after finishing a task, review or session to grade the work honestly. Scores it on two axes, forces a devil's-advocate pass against score inflation and keeps scores across sessions.

engineering.name: ship-gate
engineering.description: Use before deploying or going live ('am I ready to ship', 'can I deploy', 'preflight check'). Scans the codebase with ship_gate_scanner.py across security, database, deploy, AI, dependencies and observability, and blocks on critical items.

engineering.name: skill-security-auditor
engineering.description: Use before installing any skill or plugin from an untrusted source, or when asked if a skill is safe. Scans scripts, SKILL.md and dependencies for exfiltration, dangerous calls and prompt injection with skill_security_auditor.py.

engineering.name: skill-tester
engineering.description: Use when authoring or auditing a skill in this ecosystem, before release. Validates structure with skill_validator.py, runs its scripts with script_tester.py and grades quality and security with quality_scorer.py and security_scorer.py.

engineering.name: slo-architect
engineering.description: Use when defining or reviewing SLOs, SLIs, error budgets or burn-rate alerts. Designs SLOs with slo_designer.py, computes budgets and multi-window burn-rate thresholds with error_budget_calculator.py and catches common SLO bugs with slo_review.py.

engineering.name: spec-driven-workflow
engineering.description: Use when a feature should be specified before coding (acceptance criteria, spec-first, tests from specs). Writes the spec with spec_generator.py, checks it with spec_validator.py and extracts tests with test_extractor.py.

engineering.name: sql-database-assistant
engineering.description: Use for writing or optimizing SQL, exploring a schema, generating migrations or working with Prisma, Drizzle, TypeORM or SQLAlchemy. Analyzes queries with query_optimizer.py and schemas with schema_explorer.py.

engineering.name: tc-tracker
engineering.description: Use when tracking technical changes as records, or handing work between AI sessions with a change record. Creates, updates and validates change records with tc_create.py, tc_update.py and tc_validator.py.

engineering.name: tech-debt-tracker
engineering.description: Use when asked about tech debt, refactoring priority, a cleanup sprint or legacy modernization. Scans the code with debt_scanner.py, ranks items with debt_prioritizer.py and tracks trends with debt_dashboard.py.

engineering.name: agent-harness
engineering.description: Use when an agent should drive a goal in one of this repo's domains to a verified close, before starting the work. Compiles the goal into a task plan with goal_compiler.py and runs it through loop_controller.py, which verifies each task, caps retries and escalates.

engineering.name: agent-memory
engineering.description: Use when an agent keeps relearning the same correction, CLAUDE.md has grown unreadable, or you need to trace where a remembered rule came from. Promotes facts through four tiers only on recurrence across sessions and days, with memory_promote.py and a human adopt step.

engineering.name: agenthub
engineering.description: Use when a task should be attempted by several agents in parallel and the best result kept (code speed, copy variants, research angles). Spawns N agents in git worktrees, ranks results by metric or judge with result_ranker.py and merges the winner.

engineering.name: board
engineering.description: Use to post or read messages on the AgentHub coordination board between competing agents.

engineering.name: eval
engineering.description: Use to score and pick a winner among finished AgentHub agents by metric or judge.

engineering.name: hub-init
engineering.description: Use for /hub-init, or to start an AgentHub competition: task, agent count and evaluation criteria.

engineering.name: hub-run
engineering.description: Use for /hub-run, or to run a whole AgentHub competition end to end: init, baseline, spawn, eval and merge.

engineering.name: hub-status
engineering.description: Use for /hub-status, or to check AgentHub agent progress, branches and DAG state.

engineering.name: merge
engineering.description: Use to land the winning AgentHub branch, archive the others and clean up worktrees.

engineering.name: spawn
engineering.description: Use to launch the competing agents for an initialized AgentHub session in isolated worktrees.

engineering.name: ar-loop
engineering.description: Use for /ar-loop, or to run an autoresearch experiment on a schedule (10 min to monthly) with CronCreate.

engineering.name: ar-resume
engineering.description: Use for /ar-resume, or to continue a paused autoresearch experiment from its branch and results history.

engineering.name: ar-run
engineering.description: Use for /ar-run, or to run one manual autoresearch iteration: edit, evaluate, keep or discard.

engineering.name: ar-status
engineering.description: Use for /ar-status, or to see an autoresearch experiment's results, active loops and progress.

engineering.name: autoresearch-agent
engineering.description: Use when a file should be improved against a measurable metric (speed, bundle size, pass rate, prompt or headline score), before hand-tuning it. Loops edit, run_experiment.py, keep or git reset on a fixed evaluator; needs an eval command and a git repo.

engineering.name: setup
engineering.description: Use for /autoresearch-agent:setup, or to start a new autoresearch experiment: target, eval command, metric, direction, evaluator.

engineering.name: behuman
engineering.description: Use when the user asks for less robotic, more human replies ('be real', 'talk like a person', 'mirror mode'), or the conversation is emotionally heavy (grief, job loss, fear). Drops lists and hedging for a direct, warm voice. Not for code or factual lookups.

engineering.name: book-to-skill
engineering.description: Use when turning a book, docs folder or spec collection (PDF, EPUB, DOCX, HTML, Markdown) into an agent skill, before summarizing it by hand. Extracts with extract_document.py, compiles chapters, glossary and cheatsheet, validates with book_skill_validator.py and enforces a rights gate.

engineering.name: boost-asio-pro
engineering.description: Use for any C++ networking code with Boost.Asio or standalone Asio (TCP/UDP, SSL, timers, strands, io_context, co_spawn, awaitable, completion handlers), before writing or reviewing it. Applies lifetime, strand and cancellation rules that avoid the classic async bugs.

engineering.name: claude-coach
engineering.description: Use when the user wants to get better at using Claude ('coach me', 'teach me Claude tricks', 'make me a power user'). Rates their prompts with prompt_rater.py and surfaces one relevant power-user tip per turn after activation.

engineering.name: code-tour
engineering.description: Use when asked for a CodeTour .tour file or a step-by-step code walkthrough (onboarding, architecture, PR review, how X works). Writes persona-targeted steps that link to real files and line numbers, checked to exist.

engineering.name: collab-proof
engineering.description: Use for /collab-proof or a session retrospective on what Claude contributed versus what the user drove. Builds an evidence-backed split of the session's decisions and work.

engineering.name: data-quality-auditor
engineering.description: Use before analysis or model training on any dataset, or when asked to profile data or hunt missing values and outliers. Profiles it with data_profiler.py, missing_value_analyzer.py and outlier_detector.py and writes a remediation plan.

engineering.name: deep-learning-book
engineering.description: Use when studying or applying Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville's Deep Learning, or asking if its advice still holds. Indexes all 20 chapters with a 2016-to-2026 delta, plans reading paths with reading_path_planner.py and diagnoses training failures with training_diagnostics.py.

engineering.name: demo-video
engineering.description: Use when asked for a demo video, product walkthrough, feature showcase or GIF from screenshots or scene descriptions. Orchestrates playwright, ffmpeg and edge-tts to render it.

engineering.name: docker-development
engineering.description: Use for any Dockerfile or docker-compose file to write, optimize or review, before editing it. Checks layers, caching, size and security with dockerfile_analyzer.py and validates compose files with compose_validator.py.

engineering.name: grill-me
engineering.description: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".

engineering.name: grill-with-docs
engineering.description: Use when a plan should be stress-tested against the project's own docs (CONTEXT.md glossary, docs/adr decisions), or the user says 'grill with docs'. Scans ADRs with adr_scanner.py and updates the docs inline as terms and decisions settle.

engineering.name: handoff
engineering.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up, referencing existing artifacts (PRDs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs) by path or URL instead of duplicating them. Use whenever the user wants to hand off to a fresh agent, is ending a session mid-task, asks for a handoff doc or a summary of state, decisions and next steps for the next session, or starts a new session that picks up prior work.

engineering.name: helm-chart-builder
engineering.description: Use for any Helm chart to create, review or harden (values.yaml, templates, subcharts, RBAC, pod security), before editing it. Analyzes the chart with chart_analyzer.py and validates values with values_validator.py.

engineering.name: hivemind
engineering.description: Use when delegating grunt work to free opencode workers instead of spending Claude tokens: one worker or a scout, coder and tester swarm in worktrees. Triggers on 'spawn a worker', 'swarm', 'delegate to opencode' or /oc.

engineering.name: human-gate
engineering.description: Use before shipping anything that needs human sign-off (a plan, spec, report, page, migration or irreversible action). Builds a review page with review_page_builder.py and runs human_gate.py, which refuses to close with an open blocker or no named reviewer.

engineering.name: karpathy-coder
engineering.description: Use before committing or while reviewing a diff, or when code may be overbuilt. Checks it against Karpathy's four principles with complexity_checker.py, diff_surgeon.py and assumption_linter.py: surface assumptions, keep it simple, change surgically, verify goals.

engineering.name: llm-cost-optimizer
engineering.description: Use whenever an LLM feature is being built or its costs come up (model choice, prompt caching, token limits, per-feature spend). Sets routing, caching, max_tokens and cost logging before launch rather than after the bill.

engineering.name: llm-wiki
engineering.description: Use when building or maintaining an Obsidian second brain that an LLM keeps up to date, or when ingesting a paper, article or book into it. Ingests with ingest_source.py, maintains index and links and checks the vault with lint_wiki.py.

engineering.name: memory-engineering
engineering.description: Use before adding memory to an agent or when a memory store keeps growing (long context vs RAG vs graph vs agentic memory, what to expire). Prices the design with memory_cost_profiler.py and refuses one without a forgetting policy via forgetting_policy_linter.py.

engineering.name: minimalist
engineering.description: Use when asked to avoid over-engineering, cut dependencies or write the least code. Applies a strict ladder before any new code: YAGNI, reuse, stdlib, native platform, existing deps.

engineering.name: prompt-governance
engineering.description: Use when prompts run in production and need versioning, a registry, A/B tests, regression checks or an eval pipeline. Sets up the release process for prompts; single-prompt quality: senior-prompt-engineer.

engineering.name: security-guidance
engineering.description: Use when installing or tuning the PreToolUse security hook that warns before Claude writes command injection, XSS, SQL injection, unsafe deserialization, eval or GitHub Actions injection. Warns once per file and rule; ENABLE_SECURITY_REMINDER=0 turns it off.

engineering.name: skill-retro
engineering.description: Use when the user wants their skills graded from real session history, asks which installed skills actually work, or wants evidence-backed skill edits. Collects local sessions with collect_sessions.py, scores them against two rubrics and gates edits with score_aggregator.py.

engineering.name: skillopt-sleep
engineering.description: Use when the user wants their Claude agent to self-improve from past usage, asks about a nightly/offline 'sleep' or 'dream' cycle, memory/skill consolidation, or says things like 'make my agent better the more I use it', 'review my past sessions', 'learn my preferences', 'consolidate what you learned', 'run the sleep cycle', or wants to schedule offline self-optimization. Drives the skillopt_sleep engine: harvest past sessions → mine recurring tasks → replay offline → consolidate validated CLAUDE.md and SKILL.md behind a held-out gate.

engineering.name: spinning-up-deep-rl
engineering.description: Use when learning or applying deep RL from OpenAI's Spinning Up: MDPs, policy gradients, VPG, TRPO, PPO, DDPG, TD3, SAC, debugging RL code that fails silently, or multi-seed experiments. Indexes the 20 chapters for on-demand reading.

engineering.name: statistical-analyst
engineering.description: Use when checking whether a difference is real (A/B results, hypothesis tests) or sizing an experiment, before declaring a winner. Runs tests with hypothesis_tester.py, intervals with confidence_interval.py and sample sizes with sample_size_calculator.py.

engineering.name: strict-api
engineering.description: Use when the user says 'no hallucinations', 'verify APIs' or 'don't invent functions', or code depends on a library version you have not checked. Requires proof that every method, import and variable exists in the installed version before using it.

engineering.name: terraform-patterns
engineering.description: Use for any Terraform module, state backend, provider setup or IaC security review, before editing .tf files. Analyzes modules with tf_module_analyzer.py and scans for misconfigurations with tf_security_scanner.py.

engineering.name: universal-scraping-architect
engineering.description: Use for web scraping, crawling, document extraction or API parsing pipelines that must validate what they extract. Builds the extractor with Firecrawl or local Python and checks output with validate_extraction.py.

engineering.name: workflow-builder
engineering.description: Use when writing or running a Claude Code Workflow-tool script (.js in .claude/workflows/) for fan-out, pipeline, loop or judge-panel sub-agents. Gathers intent with workflow_intake.py, scaffolds with scaffold_workflow.py and validates with validate_workflow.py.

engineering.name: write-a-skill
engineering.description: Create new agent skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and bundled resources. Use when user wants to create, write, build, or author a new skill.

engineering.name: zero-hallucination-coder
engineering.description: Use before high-stakes or multi-file coding (auth, databases, migrations), or when asked to plan carefully and avoid invented APIs. Runs discuss, map, decompose, execute and verify, checking every import and API exists. Not for trivial edits.

engineering-team.name: adversarial-reviewer
engineering-team.description: Use before merging a PR or when a self-review feels too agreeable and the change needs a genuinely critical read. Reviews the diff through hostile reviewer personas that catch blind spots the author and a friendly reviewer share.

engineering-team.name: ai-security
engineering-team.description: Use when assessing an AI/ML system or LLM agent for prompt injection, jailbreaks, model inversion, data poisoning or tool abuse. Maps findings to MITRE ATLAS and scores robustness with ai_threat_scanner.py.

engineering-team.name: aws-solution-architect
engineering-team.description: Use when designing or costing an AWS architecture (serverless, Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, ECS, Aurora, CloudFormation, migration to AWS). Designs it with architecture_designer.py, generates stacks with serverless_stack.py and finds savings with cost_optimizer.py.

engineering-team.name: azure-cloud-architect
engineering-team.description: Use when designing or costing an Azure architecture (AKS, App Service, Functions, Cosmos DB, Bicep or ARM, Azure DevOps, migration to Azure). Designs it with architecture_designer.py, generates Bicep with bicep_generator.py and finds savings with cost_optimizer.py.

engineering-team.name: cloud-security
engineering-team.description: Use when checking AWS, Azure or GCP for security misconfigurations: IAM privilege escalation, public buckets, open security groups, IaC gaps. Runs cloud_posture_check.py and maps findings to MITRE ATT&CK.

engineering-team.name: code-reviewer
engineering-team.description: Use for any code review: a pull request, a diff, a commit, or a pasted function, handler or file in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Swift, Kotlin, C#/.NET, Java, C, C++, Rust, Ruby, PHP or Dart/Flutter. Applies per-language rule packs (security such as SQL injection and missing auth, async and resource handling, error handling, performance) and scripts that score a PR's risk and complexity, then gives a merge verdict with blocking and non-blocking findings. Use whenever the user asks to review, check or look over code, says 'code review', 'review this PR', 'review this diff' or 'is this safe to merge', or asks what is wrong with a snippet, even a single function.

engineering-team.name: email-template-builder
engineering-team.description: Use when adding or reworking transactional email (React Email templates, Resend, Postmark, SendGrid or SES, preview, i18n, dark mode, deliverability). Builds the template system and provider integration end to end.

engineering-team.name: embedded-iot-mentor
engineering-team.description: Use for any embedded or IoT hardware project (ESP32, STM32, Arduino, Pico, firmware, PCB, MQTT, Home Assistant, sensor dashboards), before buying parts. Picks the MCU, board and toolchain, decides where readings go and gives a phased build plan with time and cost.

engineering-team.name: engineering-skills
engineering-team.description: Use when looking for which engineering-team skill fits a task (architecture, frontend, backend, QA, DevOps, security, AI/ML, data, cloud). Lists them and routes to one; load only that skill.

engineering-team.name: epic-design
engineering-team.description: Use for any landing page, hero section or scroll-driven web design that should feel cinematic (parallax, scrollytelling, overlapping sections, text reveals, Apple-style animation), before coding. Inspects assets with inspect-assets.py, then builds with 45+ 2.5D techniques, no WebGL.

engineering-team.name: gcp-cloud-architect
engineering-team.description: Use when designing or costing a Google Cloud architecture (Cloud Run, GKE, Functions, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, migration to GCP). Designs it with architecture_designer.py, deploys with deployment_manager.py and finds savings with cost_optimizer.py.

engineering-team.name: incident-commander
engineering-team.description: Use when declaring or running a production incident or outage, or writing its post-incident review. Classifies severity with incident_classifier.py, rebuilds the timeline with timeline_reconstructor.py and drafts the PIR with pir_generator.py. Security incidents: incident-response.

engineering-team.name: incident-response
engineering-team.description: Use when a security incident is detected or suspected and needs triage, SEV1-SEV4 classification, escalation and forensic evidence collection. Runs incident_triage.py and follows the NIST SP 800-61 lifecycle. Outages: incident-commander.

engineering-team.name: ms365-tenant-manager
engineering-team.description: Use for Microsoft 365 tenant administration (Entra ID users, Exchange Online, Teams, licenses, Conditional Access, compliance reports). Plans setup with tenant_setup.py, bulk-manages users with user_management.py and generates PowerShell with powershell_generator.py.

engineering-team.name: named-persona-adversarial-review
engineering-team.description: Use when a PR has architectural or UX impact, or automated review feels generic, and you want it reviewed through named engineers' documented views (Torvalds, Thompson, Carmack, Beck, Jobs, Cagan). Cites the source for each persona's critique.

engineering-team.name: red-green-proof
engineering-team.description: Turns a suspected bug into a proven one. Verify the cause against reality before claiming it, write a test that FAILS on the current code, apply the fix, watch it pass — then revert the fix and confirm the test goes red again, because a test that passes both ways proves nothing. Invoked bare after a debugging conversation, it takes the target from context rather than asking. Use when fixing a bug, investigating an incident, hardening a flaky area, or when asked to "add tests that reveal the bug". Triggers on "/red-green-proof", "prove the bug", "red-green", "make the test fail first", "is that test load-bearing", "reveal the bug with a test".

engineering-team.name: red-team
engineering-team.description: Use when planning or running an authorized red team engagement or attack path analysis. Plans the kill chain with engagement_planner.py: MITRE ATT&CK techniques, choke points, OPSEC risk and crown jewels.

engineering-team.name: security-pen-testing
engineering-team.description: Use for an authorized penetration test, vulnerability scan or OWASP Top 10 check of an app or API. Scans with vulnerability_scanner.py, audits dependencies with dependency_auditor.py and writes the report with pentest_report_generator.py.

engineering-team.name: senior-architect
engineering-team.description: Use for system architecture decisions (monolith vs microservices, database choice, scalability, ADRs, design reviews) or architecture diagrams. Analyzes dependencies with dependency_analyzer.py, assesses the project with project_architect.py and draws Mermaid or PlantUML with architecture_diagram_generator.py.

engineering-team.name: senior-backend
engineering-team.description: Use for backend work: REST or GraphQL APIs, auth, microservices, PostgreSQL queries, migrations or load tests. Decides with backend_decision_engine.py, scaffolds with api_scaffolder.py, migrates with database_migration_tool.py and load-tests with api_load_tester.py.

engineering-team.name: senior-computer-vision
engineering-team.description: Use for computer vision work: object detection, segmentation, training a custom model, or optimizing and deploying inference (YOLO, DETR, SAM, ONNX, TensorRT). Builds datasets with dataset_pipeline_builder.py, trains with vision_model_trainer.py and tunes inference with inference_optimizer.py.

engineering-team.name: senior-data-engineer
engineering-team.description: Use for data pipelines and ETL or ELT (Spark, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, data modeling, data quality). Orchestrates with pipeline_orchestrator.py, validates with data_quality_validator.py and tunes jobs with etl_performance_optimizer.py.

engineering-team.name: senior-data-scientist

c-level-advisor.name: cro-advisor

c-level-advisor.name: culture-architect

c-level-advisor.name: decision-logger

c-level-advisor.name: founder-coach

c-level-advisor.name: general-counsel-advisor

c-level-advisor.name: internal-narrative

c-level-advisor.name: intl-expansion

c-level-advisor.name: ma-playbook

c-level-advisor.name: org-health-diagnostic

c-level-advisor.name: scenario-war-room

c-level-advisor.name: strategic-alignment

c-level-advisor.name: vpe-advisor

c-level-advisor.name: board-prep

c-level-advisor.name: challenge

c-level-advisor.name: executive-mentor
c-level-advisor.description: Use when a founder or executive needs a plan stress-tested, a dreaded decision made, a hard board meeting prepared or an honest post-mortem. Adversarial thinking partner; scores options with decision_matrix_scorer.py and maps stakeholders with stakeholder_mapper.py.

c-level-advisor.name: hard-call
c-level-advisor.description: Use for a decision where every option hurts (layoff vs down round, killing a loved product). Runs 10/10/10 and regret minimization.

c-level-advisor.name: postmortem

c-level-advisor.name: stress-test
c-level-advisor.description: Use before betting on a plan whose core assumptions are unvalidated (a hockey-stick model, a long enterprise pilot).

project-management.name: senior-pm

project-management.name: team-communications

ra-qm-team.name: agent-decision-receipts

ra-qm-team.name: capa-officer

ra-qm-team.name: cmmc-readiness

ra-qm-team.name: eu-ai-act-specialist

ra-qm-team.name: fda-consultant-specialist
ra-qm-team.description: Use for FDA medical device questions: 510(k) vs De Novo vs PMA, predicates and substantial equivalence, QMSR (21 CFR 820), HIPAA or device cybersecurity. Runs fda_submission_tracker.py, qsr_compliance_checker.py and hipaa_risk_assessment.py.

ra-qm-team.name: gdpr-dsgvo-expert
ra-qm-team.description: Use for GDPR or DSGVO work: scanning a codebase for privacy risks, writing a DPIA or tracking data subject requests against the Art. 12(3) deadline. Runs gdpr_compliance_checker.py, dpia_generator.py and data_subject_rights_tracker.py; final calls go to the DPO.

ra-qm-team.name: information-security-manager-iso27001

ra-qm-team.name: isms-audit-expert

ra-qm-team.name: iso42001-specialist
ra-qm-team.description: Use for ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system work: gap analysis against Clauses 4-10, the AI risk register and Annex A controls, or the internal audit plan. Runs aims_gap_analyzer.py, ai_risk_register_builder.py and aims_audit_scheduler.py.

ra-qm-team.name: mdr-745-specialist
ra-qm-team.description: Use for EU MDR 2017/745 work: device classification under Annex VIII, technical file gaps (Annex II/III), clinical evaluation, PMS and PSUR cadence, notified body prep. Checks the file with mdr_gap_analyzer.py.

ra-qm-team.name: qms-audit-expert
ra-qm-team.description: Use for ISO 13485 internal audits: planning the program, running an audit, classifying findings or preparing for an external audit. Optimizes the schedule with audit_schedule_optimizer.py.

ra-qm-team.name: quality-documentation-manager
ra-qm-team.description: Use for QMS document control: numbering, versioning, change control or 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures. Validates documents with document_validator.py and tracks versions with document_version_control.py.

ra-qm-team.name: quality-manager-qmr

ra-qm-team.name: quality-manager-qms-iso13485

ra-qm-team.name: ra-qm-skills

ra-qm-team.name: regulatory-affairs-head

ra-qm-team.name: risk-management-specialist

ra-qm-team.name: soc2-compliance

business-growth.name: revenue-operations

business-growth.description: Use for pre-sales work: RFP coverage gaps, competitive feature matrices or planning and scoring a proof of concept. Runs rfp_response_analyzer.py, competitive_matrix_builder.py and poc_planner.py.

finance.name: financial-analyst

finance.name: month-end-close
finance.description: Use when running, planning or speeding up a month-end (or quarter-end) close — building or reviewing the close checklist and calendar, reconciling a bank statement or sub-ledger to the general ledger, writing or reviewing flux (variance) explanations, or finding why the close takes too many days. finance.name: passive-deal-screener

finance.name: saas-metrics-coach

finance.name: stock-analysis

finance.name: business-investment-advisor
finance.description: Use when deciding whether a capital expense is worth it (equipment, property, an acquisition, hiring, technology), or for ROI, IRR, NPV, payback, build vs buy or lease vs buy.

productivity.name: andreessen
productivity.description: Use when the user wants a blunt market-first verdict on an idea, venture or career bet ('is there a market', 'are we at PMF', 'pmarca mode'), or a 3x5-card daily plan. productivity.name: capture
productivity.description: Use whenever the user unloads a messy brain dump of ideas, tasks and plans ('capture this', 'brain dump', a long unstructured paste) and wants it organized. Sorts it with dump_classifier.py into projects, tasks and connections with nothing lost.

productivity.name: deep-work
productivity.description: Use when someone wants to plan a deep work day, time-block their calendar or task list, budget or cut shallow work, protect focus hours, track deep-work sessions and streaks, run an end-of-day shutdown ritual, or says "/deep-work" or "/time-block". productivity.name: inbox-setup
productivity.description: Use when setting up email triage for the first time, before inbox-triage, or when priorities change. Interviews the user one question at a time and writes the knowledge base inbox-triage reads, validated with kb_validator.py.

productivity.name: inbox-triage

productivity.name: fable-goal
productivity.description: Use when the user wants a /goal prompt rather than the build itself ('/fable-goal', 'turn this into a goal prompt', 'write the prompt that builds X'). Turns their ramble into one copy-paste prompt checked by goal_prompt_self_check.py.

productivity.name: session-handoff
productivity.description: Write a handoff document so a fresh session or another agent can pick up exactly where this one left off: goal, current state, decisions, next steps and the skills to load, referencing existing files instead of copying them, with secrets redacted before saving. Use whenever the user is ending a session, switching machines, running low on context, or asks for a handoff, a handoff doc, a 'pick up where we left off' summary, or to compact the conversation for next time. Saves to a location the user picks on first run (OS temp, home folder or per-project .handoff/) and can auto-load the latest handoff at the next session start.

productivity.name: meetings
productivity.description: Use when someone wants to decide whether a meeting is worth calling, price a meeting in dollars, build a timeboxed agenda with desired outcomes, or turn messy meeting notes into owned action items — or says "should this be a meeting", "/cs-meeting-prep", or "/cs-meeting-actions". Runs a cost gate (ASYNC / NOT-READY / MEET), builds a decision-first agenda, and extracts an owner + due-date checklist that flags every orphan.

productivity.name: reflect
productivity.description: Use when the user says 'step back', 'zoom out', 'are we on track' or 'sanity check this', or work has gone deep into details without a check on direction. Reassesses direction, assumptions and bias across five dimensions.

productivity.name: roast
productivity.description: Use when someone asks to roast an idea, pressure-test or stress-test an idea, validate a business idea, "convene the panel", get a brutal second opinion before building something, or says "/roast". productivity.name: swedish-mentor

productivity.name: weekly-review

commercial.name: commercial-forecaster
commercial.description: Use when building a bookings, ARR, pipeline or NRR forecast, or a commit, best-case and pipeline board number. Forecasts with bookings_forecaster.py, projects cohorts with cohort_arr_projector.py and scores stage confidence with funnel_confidence_scorer.py, showing every conversion assumption.

commercial.name: commercial-policy
commercial.description: Use when writing or revising discount rules: discount matrix, approver thresholds, exception flows and the deal framework sales works under. Builds the matrix with discount_matrix_builder.py, routes exceptions with exception_router.py and checks the policy with policy_linter.py.

commercial.name: commercial-skills
commercial.description: Use when a commercial request needs routing (pricing, deal review, discounts, partners, channels, policy, RFPs, forecasts): 'review this deal', 'should we discount'. Lists the commercial skills and routes to one.

commercial.name: deal-desk
commercial.description: Use before closing a deal that needs a discount beyond AE authority, has a redlined MSA or unclear per-deal economics. Scores it with deal_scorer.py, names approvers with discount_approval_router.py and flags risky terms with terms_redliner.py. Never auto-approves.

commercial.name: partnerships-architect
commercial.description: Use when deciding whether to sign a partner, at which tier (referral, reseller, OEM, SI, alliance), with what joint GTM and revshare. Runs partner_tier_classifier.py, revshare_modeler.py and joint_gtm_planner.py.

commercial.name: pricing-strategist
commercial.description: Use when choosing or revisiting pricing: seat, usage, value-based, freemium or hybrid, Van Westendorp willingness-to-pay analysis, or Good/Better/Best tiers. Runs pricing_model_picker.py, wtp_analyzer.py and packaging_designer.py and returns a range, not one number.

commercial.name: rfp-responder
commercial.description: Use when an RFP, RFI, RFQ or security or vendor questionnaire arrives. Parses mandatory vs weighted requirements with rfp_parser.py, drafts proof-point answers with response_drafter.py and estimates win chance with winrate_predictor.py.

research-ops.name: clinical-research
research-ops.description: Use when designing a prospective clinical study: choosing primary and secondary endpoints, estimating sample size and power, or scoring feasibility before submission. Runs endpoint_selector.py, sample_size_estimator.py and phase_gate_scorer.py; outputs are estimates for a biostatistician to confirm.

research-ops.name: interview-mapper
research-ops.description: Use when coding or making sense of one interview transcript (customer, JTBD, expert, usability, exit). Extracts verbatim-grounded nuggets with extract_nuggets.py, verifies quotes with verify_quotes.py and checks conclusions hold across reruns with consensus.py.

research-ops.name: market-research
research-ops.description: Use for market sizing (TAM, SAM, SOM both top-down and bottom-up), survey sample sizes or segment scoring. Runs market_sizer.py, sample_size_planner.py and segmentation_scorer.py and never returns one unsourced number.

research-ops.name: product-research
research-ops.description: Use when planning or synthesizing user research: choosing the method, deciding how many participants, or turning coded notes into insights. Runs study_designer.py, saturation_planner.py and insight_synthesizer.py, which refuses single-source insights.

research-ops.name: research-finance
research-ops.description: Use for R&D program money: multi-period budgets with indirect cost split, burn and runway against milestones, or capitalize vs expense routing. Runs program_budget_planner.py, burn_runway_tracker.py and capex_vs_opex_router.py.

research-ops.name: research-ops-skills
research-ops.description: Use when an enterprise research request needs routing (clinical study design, R&D finance, market sizing, user research): 'what sample size', 'R&D budget'. Lists the research-ops skills and routes to one.

compliance-os.name: ai-act-readiness
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:ai-act-readiness, or EU AI Act readiness questions during AI-system intake or before EU deployment.

compliance-os.name: aims-audit
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:aims-audit, or ISO 42001 readiness before stage 1 or an internal audit cycle.

compliance-os.name: compliance-os
compliance-os.description: Use when running several compliance frameworks at once: which apply, where controls overlap, a mock audit or one evidence checklist. Runs framework_selector.py, cross_framework_mapper.py, audit_simulator.py and evidence_pool_generator.py.

compliance-os.name: compliance-readiness
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:compliance-readiness, or before adding a framework or planning the annual audit calendar.

compliance-os.name: fda-qsr-audit-prep
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:fda-qsr-audit-prep, or before an FDA inspection, QMSR internal audit or Form 483 response.

compliance-os.name: gdpr-audit-prep
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:gdpr-audit-prep, or before a GDPR review, post-breach audit or DPA investigation.

compliance-os.name: iso13485-audit-prep
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:iso13485-audit-prep, or before an ISO 13485 internal audit or DHF closure.

compliance-os.name: iso27001-audit-prep
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:iso27001-audit-prep, or before an ISO 27001 internal, surveillance or stage 1 audit.

compliance-os.name: soc2-audit-prep
compliance-os.description: Use for /compliance-os:soc2-audit-prep, or before or during a SOC 2 Type II observation period.

markdown-html.name: design-system
markdown-html.description: Use when setting up brand settings before the first markdown-to-HTML conversion, or changing them. Runs a 10-question onboarding with onboard.py (colors, fonts, style, TOC) and refuses palettes that fail WCAG AA via brand_palette_validator.py.

markdown-html.name: markdown-html-orchestrator
markdown-html.description: Use when the user wants a markdown file turned into a single-file interactive HTML page (document, code review or slide deck). Classifies it with doctype_classifier.py and routes to md-document, md-review or md-slides.

markdown-html.name: md-document
markdown-html.description: Use when converting long-form markdown (spec, RFC, report, plan) into a single-file HTML page with sticky TOC, search and code-copy. Parses with markdown_parser.py and renders with html_renderer.py using the design-system brand.

markdown-html.name: md-review
markdown-html.description: Use when converting a markdown code review with diff blocks and severity callouts into a two-column HTML review. Parses diffs with diff_parser.py and annotations with annotation_extractor.py; requires a named reviewer.

markdown-html.name: md-slides
markdown-html.description: Use when converting a markdown deck into a single-file HTML presentation with keyboard navigation, presenter notes and print-to-PDF. Splits slides with slide_splitter.py and renders with deck_html_renderer.py.

agent-launcher.name: agent-launcher-orchestrator
agent-launcher.description: Use when someone wants to build, launch, grade or schedule a Claude Managed Agent in their own Anthropic account ('build me an agent', 'run this nightly'). Reads the session goal, routes with goal_router.py and compiles the loop with loop_compiler.py.

agent-launcher.name: grade-iterate
agent-launcher.description: Use when a launched managed agent needs grading against a rubric and improving ('grade my agent', 'is it good enough'). Builds the outcome with outcome_builder.py, reads verdicts with verdict_reader.py and runs held-back evals from eval_scaffold.py.

agent-launcher.name: interview
agent-launcher.description: Use when someone has an agent idea to scope before launch ('help me scope an agent'). Interviews them about the one job and writes a build sheet with build_sheet_builder.py, checked by primitives_validator.py; no API key needed.

agent-launcher.name: run-without-you
agent-launcher.description: Use when a graded managed agent should run on a schedule, on an event trigger or on demand ('run it every morning'). Validates cron with cron_validator.py and builds the deployment with deployment_builder.py.

agent-launcher.name: stage-launch
agent-launcher.description: Use when a managed-agent build sheet is ready to launch ('launch it', 'deploy the agent'). Generates and validates API payloads with payload_generator.py and payload_validator.py and writes a resumable curl script with launch_script_writer.py that uses the user's own key.

agent-launcher.name: wrap-up
agent-launcher.description: Use when closing out a launched managed agent ('wrap up', 'what do I own now'). Inventories primitives with primitives_inventory.py, regenerates the overview with overview_page.py and suggests next upgrades with upgrade_suggester.py.

c-level-agents.name: boardroom
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:boardroom, or a decision spanning several executive domains (a pricing change, raise vs cut). Runs a 6-phase C-suite deliberation and writes a board memo.

c-level-agents.name: brief
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:brief, or to frame a strategic question (options, assumptions, success criteria) as a one-page brief before deliberation.

c-level-agents.name: c-level-agents
c-level-agents.description: Use when the founder wants a virtual executive team or a /c-level-agents command. Lists the 13 C-suite agents and 21 commands and routes multi-role decisions.

c-level-agents.name: caio-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:caio-review, or to challenge a plan involving AI (no eval set, API vs fine-tune vs self-host, EU AI Act class).

c-level-agents.name: cco-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cco-review, or to challenge a plan touching retention, segmentation or CS headcount.

c-level-agents.name: cdo-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cdo-review, or to challenge a plan touching training-data rights, data architecture or data monetization.

c-level-agents.name: cfo-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cfo-review, or to challenge a plan that commits real money (a hiring wave, a raise, a channel budget).

c-level-agents.name: ciso-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:ciso-review, or to challenge a plan touching customer data, compliance or production access.

c-level-agents.name: cmo-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cmo-review, or to challenge positioning, ICP, messaging or channel mix before a launch.

c-level-agents.name: cpo-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cpo-review, or to challenge a roadmap, a PMF claim or a feature-kill decision.

c-level-agents.name: cro-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cro-review, or to challenge a forecast, win-rate drop or sales-team scale-up.

c-level-agents.name: cross-eval
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cross-eval, or when a high-stakes memo needs independent review by several models before the boardroom.

c-level-agents.name: cto-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:cto-review, or to challenge an architecture commitment, a 10x scaling plan or rebuild vs buy.

c-level-agents.name: decide
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:decide, or right after the founder approves a boardroom memo, to log it as a durable decision.

c-level-agents.name: execute
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:execute, or to turn an approved decision into a 90-day plan with weekly milestones and owners.

c-level-agents.name: founder-mode
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:founder-mode, or any founder strategy question that hasn't been routed yet. Sends it to the right C-suite advisor or the boardroom.

c-level-agents.name: freeze
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:freeze, or to put a cooling-off lock on an irreversible decision made under pressure.

c-level-agents.name: gc-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:gc-review, or to challenge a term sheet, customer MSA, IP assignment or regulatory exposure before signing.

c-level-agents.name: office-hours
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:office-hours, or when a founder question is too vague to route. Asks six YC-style questions before any advice.

c-level-agents.name: onboard
c-level-agents.description: Use for /cs-onboard, or when the virtual C-suite lacks company context. Interviews the founder and writes ~/.claude/company-context.md.

c-level-agents.name: post-mortem
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:post-mortem, or when a decision hits its 90-day review or kill criteria. Scores it against the original assumptions and dissent.

c-level-agents.name: vpe-review
c-level-agents.description: Use for /c-level-agents:vpe-review, or to challenge a plan touching delivery speed, eng hiring, team structure or on-call.

loop-library.name: loop-library
loop-library.description: Discover, find, compare, audit, repair, adapt, and design repeatable AI-agent loops with explicit triggers, actions, verification, stopping conditions, guardrails, and handoffs. Use when a user asks to analyze a codebase for potential loops, mine coding-thread history for work done more than once, turn repeated engineering work into a loop, find or recommend a published loop, create a recurring agent workflow or automation cadence, turn an outcome into a bounded copy-ready loop, or review an existing loop for weak checks, unsafe authority, unbounded repetition, stale state, or unclear stopping behavior.
